=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Baseline:** 100% share purchase, AUD 24.0m price, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law. Figures are from the Seller's documents and are unverified.

**Process note:** The Seller's cover note says these positions were "settled at principal level" and are "FINAL." That is the Seller's framing, not a basis for accepting them. Confirm the mandate with the Wattlebridge deal team before conceding anything. The Seller's "market" ranges are also unsupported and should be tested against precedent and your advisers' experience. The disclosure is also only current to 22 September 2026, so a bring-down to Completion is needed.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A materially higher cap, with the Seller's exposure sized against the risks in the data room (Bluefen, Ironquay, privacy, Riverlark). Consider an opening position at or near 100% for general warranties, with a fallback calibrated to deal team instructions and any W&I insurance.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter higher.** A 20% cap leaves known exposures above AUD 4.8m uncovered by any warranty claim, so they must be handled by specific indemnities or price.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis (0.10% of price) and AUD 250,000 basket (~1.04%), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A tipping (first-dollar) basket, so that once the threshold is passed, the whole claim is recoverable. A lower de minimis, with related claims aggregated.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** A deductible basket leaves the first AUD 250,000 of any loss with the Buyer, which matters given the known data room issues.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion, and that limit applies to all Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months for general warranties, so the Buyer covers a full audit and tax cycle after Completion. Fundamental, title and tax claims should run on a longer period (see SPA-N-014).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the blanket application.** Eighteen months is too short for general warranties and would cut off tax and title claims that surface later.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full price and limited by the statute of limitations, not 18 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title is the core of what the Buyer is paying for, and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap it.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** The documents contain no fraud carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that nothing limits liability for fraud, including fraud by the Seller or its agents. Non-reliance wording should not protect a party from its own fraud.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert.** This gap is significant; the draft as written could be read to limit fraud recovery.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]-[1.2] treat the entire data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records as disclosed.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties, with no general or data-room deemed disclosure. Disclosure should not qualify fundamental, tax or specific indemnity matters.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** A data-room disclosure would hollow out the warranties and make the Buyer carry the risk of anything it reviewed.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Delete the qualifier. Include an express pro-sandbagging clause so that the Buyer's knowledge does not prejudice its claims. This matters under NSW law because the position on sandbagging is not settled.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete and replace with pro-sandbagging wording.** The Buyer has now identified specific issues (DD-002 to DD-012), so this clause would bar claims for exactly the matters the Buyer found.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Consent "addressed"; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat it as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The disclosure confirms no final written consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:** Receipt of the final written consent and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent. Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue, so the Buyer needs a walk right or price adjustment if it is not obtained.
- **Recommendation:** **Make a condition precedent.** "Reasonable endeavours" does not protect the Buyer against losing 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release for the ~AUD 3.2m facility to be provided after Completion. The facility has not been repaid.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment and discharge of security at Completion, with the payout amount deducted from price as debt under the debt-free/cash-free mechanism. Obtain a payoff letter, a PPSR discharge, and any other security releases.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release.** The Buyer should not take the company subject to AUD 3.2m of secured debt on a promise of a later release.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are excluded from the funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax, super or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** The bonuses, plus employer on-costs and payroll tax, treated as debt-like items reducing the price, or paid by the Seller. Confirm the conditions and the tax treatment.
- **Recommendation:** **Treat as debt-like.** The company will carry this cost after Completion, and the funds flow should show it.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, which the Seller calls "adequate." DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay IP ownership and transfer risk, not only the SOW3 fee. Obtain a confirmatory assignment and evidence of payment as conditions precedent. Make the indemnity uncapped or at least price-level, with a holdback if needed.
- **Recommendation:** **Expand and make a condition.** An indemnity tied to one payment does not protect the Buyer's ownership of the IP it is buying.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material." The disclosure does not establish whether unauthorised access occurred or whether notification is required. The export may contain ~1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed forensic and privacy assessment before signing, including whether the incident is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach scheme. A specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory action and claims, a privacy compliance warranty, and possibly a holdback. Take specialist privacy advice.
- **Recommendation:** **Investigate and indemnify.** The Seller's "not material" view is unsupported by the disclosure, which itself says the investigation is preliminary.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer should want:** Read together, the three renewals should be assessed for timing and scope. Confirm whether each is terminable, whether any is accrued for pre-Completion services, and whether any is non-ordinary. Accrued or pre-Completion amounts should be debt-like.
- **Recommendation:** **Verify and treat any accrued portion as debt-like.** The Seller has not shown these are ordinary-course or terminable.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Fundamental, tax, IP and general warranties all sit under one regime with one cap, one basket and one time limit.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate categories with different regimes. Fundamental warranties and title at full price, with statute-of-limitations periods. Tax claims on a separate indemnity with a statute-plus-60-days period. IP warranties with their own cap. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, Bluefen, bonuses) sitting outside the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject a single regime.** Putting high-risk categories under the general cap and time limit is the single biggest structural problem in the Seller's draft.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures holding 100%. The disclosure notes this does not confirm the Buyer has verified title itself.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, original share certificates, all transfers in the chain, a check of the constitution for pre-emption or transfer restrictions, and PPSR searches against the shares. Title warranties should be fundamental (see SPA-N-004).
- **Recommendation:** **Verify independently before signing.** A share register is evidence of title, not verification of it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the general cap and basket, with a statute-plus-60-days time limit. Dedicated IP warranties (ownership, non-infringement, open-source, employee and contractor assignments), with their own cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The Seller has not justified folding tax and IP into the general regime, and this sits with the category problem in SPA-N-014.

---

**Priority for the next mark-up:** SPA-N-014 (category separation), SPA-N-005 (fraud carve-out), SPA-N-007 (buyer knowledge), SPA-N-006 (disclosure scope), SPA-N-008 and SPA-N-009 (conditions precedent for Bluefen and Riverlark), and SPA-N-012 (privacy investigation before signing).

This is a commercial and legal review to support your team. NSW counsel should review the final drafting, particularly the fraud, sandbagging and limitation provisions, and the privacy analysis.
